code.source:
Task A4/A6: hourly 2023 weather for Zurich/Kloten (KLO) from MeteoSwiss OGD.

Input : data/raw/meteoswiss/ogd-smn_klo_h_historical_2020-2029.csv  (SRC-004)
Output: data/canonical/weather_klo_2023_hourly.csv                   (DER-007)
        docs/data/data_quality_reports/qc_weather_klo_2023.json

Timestamp convention (D-009, determined empirically, see EL-0018): MeteoSwiss hourly
`reference_timestamp` (UTC) labels the END of the averaging hour. The value for the
hour that STARTS at UTC t is therefore the row labelled t+1h. Evidence: July mean global
radiation peaks at label 12:00 UTC while local solar noon at Kloten is ~11:26 UTC
(interval [11,12] centred 11:30).

Variables (all measured except the one derived column):
  temp_c (tre200h0), rh_pct (ure200h0), ghi_wm2 (gre000h0), diffuse_wm2 (ods000h0),
  sunshine_min (sre000h0), beam_horizontal_wm2 = ghi - diffuse   [DERIVED, horizontal
  beam component, NOT direct-normal irradiance].
No cleaning: night-time radiation of ~1-2 W/m2 (sensor offset) is kept as measured.

Run: cl/bin/python -I swiss/pipeline/build_weather.py

Inputs : data/canonical/hourly/<role>_2023_hourly.csv (DER-005), weather_klo_2023_hourly.csv (DER-007)

All thermal quantities are DERIVED (electricity x modeled COP), not measured.
Parameters (D-014d): supply T: SH 35 C (SFH floor heating) / 45 C (MFH assumption), DHW 55 C;
SPF targets (Arpagaus et al. 2023, IEA HPC paper 478, Table 1): SFH SH-only 3.7; MFH combined 3.1 (renovation
class); DHW-mode SPF 2.8 for all.  eta calibrated per building (annual).

Model M-001: Carnot-fraction heat-pump COP in CityLearn's functional form, and electricity -> heat derivation.

COP(T_out) = eta * (T_sup + 273.15) / (T_sup - T_out), values < 0 or > 20 set to 20
(identical to citylearn.energy_model.HeatPump.get_cop(heating=True), verified by a test).
Heat output of a mode = electricity * COP(T_out).  eta is calibrated so that the annual
ratio sum(heat)/sum(electricity) equals a target SPF (literature value, see parameter_registry.csv).

code.source:
Task A6 / D-013: modeled hourly consumption-based LIFECYCLE carbon intensity of the Swiss electricity supply.

Inputs : data/raw/energy_charts/*.json (SRC-011, CC BY 4.0, attribution energy-charts.info):
         public_power for ch/de/fr/at/it (MW) and cbpf (cross-border physical flows into CH, GW; positive = import into CH,
         sign convention verified: July 2023 net export of 56 GWh/day equals ch 'Cross border electricity trading').
Method (first-order tracing, average not marginal intensity):
  I_dom,t = sum_k G_k,t EF_k / sum_k G_k,t                       (Swiss domestic generation only; diagnostic series)
  I_n,t   = same formula for neighbour n (FR, DE, AT, IT) from its own generation (its own imports ignored)
  I_cons,t = [sum_k G_k,t EF_k + sum_n max(F_n,t,0) * I_n,t] / [sum_k G_k,t + sum_n max(F_n,t,0)]
  Exports leave at the average mix (do not change the intensity). Pumped-storage generation and consumption are excluded.
Emission factors: IPCC AR5 WG3 Annex III Table A.III.2 lifecycle medians (verified from the PDF) with documented PROXIES
for technologies absent from that table (see EF_PROXY). Output unit gCO2eq/kWh (and kg/kWh for CityLearn).
No interpolation: hours with missing inputs stay NaN and are counted.
Run: cl/bin/python -I swiss/pipeline/build_carbon.py [2023|2016|2017]

code.source:
Task B3: assumed-PV scenario inputs (M-003). Writes, under data/canonical/pv/:
  pv_ac_w_per_kwp_2023_hourly.csv   inverter AC output per kWp in W/kW (CityLearn solar_generation convention), 8,760 hours
  pv_capacity_2023.json             per building and yield-to-demand ratio (0.5, 1.0, 1.5): kWp, cap, binding flag, annual yield
Classification: modeled (irradiance measured, conversion modeled) + assumed-parameter badge (D-021). No building has known PV
except by survey (SFH-low: no); SFH-mid and SFH-high are unknown (ISS-021), so every building gets the SCENARIO PV and the scenario
is "with assumed PV". Annual demand = non-shiftable load + heat-pump electricity under no control (ALG-001), from DER-009.
Run: cl/bin/python -I swiss/pipeline/build_pv.py

M-003 PV yield model (Phase B, task B3), built on pvlib 0.16.1: hourly AC energy per kWp from MeteoSwiss global and diffuse irradiance.

Chain (all pvlib functions; parameters are assumptions or PVWatts defaults, see `PARAMS` and docs/models/parameter_registry.csv):
  1. `solarposition.get_solarposition` (NREL SPA) at the interval midpoint for Zurich/Kloten.
  2. Direct normal irradiance from GHI and DHI with `irradiance.dni` (no measured DNI is available, ISS-005).
  3. `irradiance.get_total_irradiance` on a south-facing plane, tilt 30 deg, Perez transposition (all-sites composite 1990),
     extraterrestrial radiation and relative airmass from pvlib, ground albedo 0.20.
  4. `temperature.sapm_cell` (open rack, glass/glass parameters), constant wind speed assumed (no wind in the weather file),
     `pvsystem.pvwatts_dc` (gamma -0.4 %/K), `pvsystem.pvwatts_losses` with the PVWatts default loss items (14.08 %), and
     `inverter.pvwatts` (nominal efficiency 0.96, DC/AC ratio 1.2 so peaks above 1/1.2 of kWp are clipped).
Not modelled: shading from the actual surroundings, horizon, snow beyond the loss item, module degradation, real wind. Results are
modeled (D-021) and depend on assumed parameters; the annual specific yield is a plausibility check, not a validation against
measured PV output.

Input timestamps are the START of the hour (UTC), as in weather_klo_2023_hourly.csv (D-009); irradiance is the hourly mean,
so the sun position is taken at start + 30 min.

code.source:
B7 step 1: what the derived heat demand can say about the single-node RC model (equation (1) of Melillo et al. 2021, J. Phys.: Conf. Ser. 2042 012009, as pasted by the owner):
    C_l dT/dt = -H (T - T_amb) + g I + L_emitter + L_internal
Quasi-steady daily regression over heating days (daily mean outdoor temperature < 12 C), where dT/dt averages out and C_l drops out:
    mean heat demand [kW] = a + b T_amb + c GHI    ->  H = -b (W/K), balance temperature = a / -b, effective solar aperture g_eff = -c (W per W/m2)
Only H and g_eff are (partly) identifiable from heat demand and weather; C_l needs indoor temperature dynamics and stays an assumption.
The heat demand is DERIVED (heat pump electricity x modeled COP, SPF-anchored, M-001), so H inherits the SPF assumption (ISS-028).
Output: data/canonical/rc/rc_quasi_steady_fit_2023.json   Run: cl/bin/python -I swiss/pipeline/fit_rc_params.py

B7: pooled per-m2 RC parameters (M-005) and per-building effective area (energy closure with the derived heat, D-038).
Output: data/canonical/rc/rc_params_2023.json   Run: cl/bin/python -I swiss/pipeline/build_rc_params.py

M-005 single-node (1R1C) building thermal model, equation (1) of Melillo et al. 2021 (J. Phys.: Conf. Ser. 2042 012009), per floor area:
    C dT/dt = -H (T - T_amb) + g I + L_emitter + L_internal
Pooled per-m2 priors (owner decision 2026-11-18): the same H, g, C and internal gain per m2 for every building; only the EFFECTIVE AREA of a
building is calibrated, so that the model with ideal control at the setpoint reproduces the building's annual derived heat demand (energy
closure; the derived heat is itself SPF-anchored, M-001, ISS-028). All priors are assumptions or unverified; the model is labelled synthetic.
The step is the exact solution for piecewise-constant inputs over one step (no integration error):
    T_{k+1} = T_inf + (T_k - T_inf) exp(-dt / tau),   tau = C / H,   T_inf = T_amb + (g I + L_internal + L_emitter) / H
Units here: power in kW, areas in m2, H in W/(K m2), C in J/(K m2), I in W/m2, time step in seconds.

code.source:
Task B2: 15-minute data pipeline for the Swiss district (2023 local year, UTC window [2022-12-31 23:00, 2023-12-31 23:00), 35,040 quarter-hours).

Everything at 15 minutes is derived from the ORIGINAL 15-minute smart-meter data wherever it exists, with the same rules as the hourly pipeline so that the
hourly series are exact aggregates of the 15-minute series (checked in qc_15min_2023.json and swiss/tests/test_q15.py):
  electricity   SFH (HEAPO): HP and other load as measured, the 24 h gap of 2023-10-29 filled from day-1 and day+1 at quarter-hour resolution (D-011, synthetic);
                MFH (EKZ): HP meter and measured common-area meters as measured, apartment composite = units x mean of the SAME seeded meters (qc_2023_buildings.json)
                at quarter-hour resolution (D-015, synthetic)
  weather       MeteoSwiss KLO is HOURLY only: temperature is held constant within the hour; global and diffuse irradiance are redistributed inside the hour with the
                shape of a Haurwitz clear-sky curve, normalised so that each hourly mean is preserved exactly (assumption A-022; no real 15-minute weather exists)
  tariff        EKZ standard tariff at its native 15-minute resolution
  carbon        modeled hourly carbon intensity held constant within the hour
  PV            same pvlib chain as hourly (M-003) with 15-minute sun positions and the redistributed irradiance
  thermal       M-001 with the hourly calibration (eta, supply temperatures from thermal_params.json) applied to quarter-hour HP electricity. A first version split the
                baseline with a quarter-hour profile; it changed the space-heating / hot-water split by up to 26 % because the split rule (minimum of electricity and a
                baseline profile) is not linear. Final rule (A-023): the hourly baseline of M-001 is distributed over the four quarters in proportion to the quarter's HP
                electricity, so every 15-minute thermal series aggregates EXACTLY to the hourly one. All thermal quantities are DERIVED.
Outputs: data/canonical/q15/ (see below) and docs/data/data_quality_reports/qc_15min_2023.json
Run: cl/bin/python -I swiss/pipeline/build_15min.py

code.source:
B8 EV charging and B6 local electricity community (LEG): labelled scenarios on S2 (assumed PV and battery), exact optima by linear program.
These are LP-level scenarios: the CityLearn environment has no EV or LEG in this dataset, so there is no replay for them (decision D-045); the physical balance of every building is
the validated S2 balance plus the EV load, and the bill identities are tested in swiss/tests/test_ev_leg.py.

EV (B8). Measured data: the EKZ EV charging station meter 198511 (an apartment building with 5 housing units, 6,428 kWh in 2023, hourly profile from the 15-minute file; 1.7 % of quarters
missing are filled with the mean of the same hour and day type). The meter aggregates several vehicles, so one EV per housing unit is ASSUMED (profile / 5, about 1,285 kWh per year per EV).
EVs are assigned to SFH-mid and SFH-high only: SFH-low's measured household electricity already contains EV charging (ISS-026), adding one would double count. Keep separate from
measured loads: the EV load is added on top of the S2 net consumption and reported separately.
Flexibility (assumed): the vehicle is plugged in every day from 17:00 to 08:00 local time; the energy the measured profile delivers inside that window must still be delivered inside
it (arrival-to-departure window, no V2G), at most 7.4 kW; charging outside the window stays as measured and fixed.
Variants per rung: no EV; EV uncontrolled (measured shape) with everything else optimised; EV flexible.

LEG (B6). Framework facts (reported from EKZ document "Voraussetzungen fuer die Bildung und die Teilnahme an einer LEG", read 2026-11-18, and DSO notices; the statutory text itself was not
read): since 1 January 2026 (StromVG art. 17d ff., StromVV art. 19e ff.), participants in one municipality, on the same grid level and supplied by the same substation, with communicating smart
meters and generation of at least 5 % of the connection power, may trade self-generated electricity freely among themselves; the grid-use tariff is discounted by 40 % on the internally
exchanged energy (20 % if a voltage transformation is needed); residual supply stays with the supplier. Physical flows are unchanged; only the financial allocation changes.
Model (assumptions, labelled): the six buildings form one LEG (they are a composite, not real neighbours); the discount delta = 0.4; in every step internal exchange s = min(sum exports,
sum imports) is allocated pro rata; buyers pay the internal price p_leg plus (1 - delta) x grid fee on the internal share instead of energy plus grid fee; sellers receive p_leg instead of the export
price; p_leg = 9 Rp/kWh (between the 8 Rp/kWh export price and the 10.35 Rp/kWh energy price, assumed). For the district total p_leg cancels: gain per internal kWh = energy price + delta x grid fee
- export price. Levies other than the grid fee and administration fees are not modelled. The joint optimum uses one program for all buildings.
Run: PYTHONPATH=. cl/bin/python swiss/experiments/oracle_ev_leg.py   Output: swiss/experiments/oracle_results/ev_leg.json and docs/experiments/validation_reports/ev_leg_scenarios.md

code.source:
Phase C, WP1: hourly climate scenarios for Zurich/Kloten from CH2025 daily data (docs/phases/phase_c_proposal_updated.md section 3).

Inputs : data/raw/ch2025_klo/ogd-climate-scenarios-ch2025_klo_<var>_<level>.csv   (MeteoSwiss & ETH Zurich 2025, CC BY 4.0; daily, 365-day calendar,
         years 0001 to 0030 are anonymous model-years, several regional-climate-model chains per file, NA = missing; variables tas, tasmin, tasmax, rsds, hurs;
         levels ref91-20, gwl1.5, gwl2.0, gwl3.0)
         data/canonical/weather_klo_2023_hourly.csv                                  (observed 2023 hourly Kloten series, UTC; DER-007)
Outputs: data/canonical/climate/weather_klo_<scenario>_hourly.csv                    same columns as the 2023 file
         data/canonical/climate/pv_ac_w_per_kwp_<scenario>_hourly.csv                scenario PV per kWp (M-003 chain of swiss/models/pv.py)
         data/canonical/climate/heatwave_spells.json                                 chosen spells and severity distributions
         docs/experiments/validation_reports/climate_scenarios.md                    generated validation report (no hand-typed numbers)
Scenarios: `hist` is the 2023 file itself (not duplicated). gwl1.5, gwl2.0, gwl3.0 = typical warmed 2023 (delta change); hist_hw, gwl2.0_hw, gwl3.0_hw =
           the same with a hot spell from the CH2025 ensemble of that level replacing the 168 rows of the 2023 test week 29 (rows 4872 to 5039).

Method (assumptions are labelled A-C1 to A-C8 in the report and in docs/phases/phase_c_drafts/wp1_registry_draft.md):
 1. Typical warmed year. Per month m (local calendar month of the row): delta of the ensemble median (over chains, model-years and days of the month) of the level
    minus the reference 1991-2020 for tas, tasmin, tasmax (additive) and rsds, hurs (ratio). Hourly temperature: T' = T + dtas_m + (dtmax_m - dtmin_m) (s_d(h) - sbar_m)
    where s_d(h) is the observed normalised diurnal position of the hour in its local day ((T - Tmin_d) / (Tmax_d - Tmin_d), 0.5 on days with a range below 1 K) and
    sbar_m its monthly mean: the monthly mean warming equals dtas and the diurnal range changes by dtmax - dtmin. Radiation: global, direct-horizontal and diffuse of
    the hour are multiplied by min(ratio, cap / ghi), cap = max(Haurwitz clear-sky hourly mean, observed value of that hour). Humidity: rh x ratio, at most 100.
 2. Hot spells. All 7-day windows inside a model-year (any chain with valid tas, tasmin, tasmax, rsds, hurs on all seven days) are ranked by mean tasmax. The target is the
    PERCENTILE (default 95) of that distribution over ALL windows of the level's ensemble; the chosen spell is the window that starts between 1 June and 25 August (so it
    lies in JJA, as week 29 does) whose severity is closest to the target (ties: first chain, year, start). It is turned into hourly values with the observed 2023
    diurnal shape of hot days (hourly maximum >= 27 C): s' = s^gamma with gamma solved so that the hourly mean equals tas, minimum tasmin and maximum tasmax;
    radiation = Haurwitz clear-sky shape scaled to the daily mean rsds (scale capped at the 99.9th percentile of the 2023 hourly ghi / clear-sky ratio), diffuse share from
    the 2023 clearness-index relation; relative humidity: constant dew point per day solved to match the daily mean hurs. The temperature and humidity of the first and
    last RAMP (6) rows of the window are blended linearly with the base series (no 10 K jump in one hour); radiation is not blended.
Run: cl/bin/python -I swiss/pipeline/build_climate.py [--percentile 95]

Model M-001: Carnot-fraction heat-pump COP in CityLearn's functional form, and electricity -> heat derivation.

code.source:
Task A6 / D-013: modeled hourly consumption-based LIFECYCLE carbon intensity of the Swiss electricity supply.

Inputs : data/raw/energy_charts/*.json (SRC-011, CC BY 4.0, attribution energy-charts.info):
         public_power for ch/de/fr/at/it (MW) and cbpf (cross-border physical flows into CH, GW; positive = import into CH,
         sign convention verified: July 2023 net export of 56 GWh/day equals ch 'Cross border electricity trading').
Method (first-order tracing, average not marginal intensity):
  I_dom,t = sum_k G_k,t EF_k / sum_k G_k,t                       (Swiss domestic generation only; diagnostic series)
  I_n,t   = same formula for neighbour n (FR, DE, AT, IT) from its own generation (its own imports ignored)
  I_cons,t = [sum_k G_k,t EF_k + sum_n max(F_n,t,0) * I_n,t] / [sum_k G_k,t + sum_n max(F_n,t,0)]
  Exports leave at the average mix (do not change the intensity). Pumped-storage generation and consumption are excluded.
Emission factors: IPCC AR5 WG3 Annex III Table A.III.2 lifecycle medians (verified from the PDF) with documented PROXIES
for technologies absent from that table (see EF_PROXY). Output unit gCO2eq/kWh (and kg/kWh for CityLearn).
No interpolation: hours with missing inputs stay NaN and are counted.
Run: cl/bin/python -I swiss/pipeline/build_carbon.py [2023|2016|2017]

code.source:
M-003 PV yield model (Phase B, task B3), built on pvlib 0.16.1: hourly AC energy per kWp from MeteoSwiss global and diffuse irradiance.

Chain (all pvlib functions; parameters are assumptions or PVWatts defaults, see `PARAMS` and docs/models/parameter_registry.csv):
  1. `solarposition.get_solarposition` (NREL SPA) at the interval midpoint for Zurich/Kloten.
  2. Direct normal irradiance from GHI and DHI with `irradiance.dni` (no measured DNI is available, ISS-005).
  3. `irradiance.get_total_irradiance` on a south-facing plane, tilt 30 deg, Perez transposition (all-sites composite 1990),
     extraterrestrial radiation and relative airmass from pvlib, ground albedo 0.20.
  4. `temperature.sapm_cell` (open rack, glass/glass parameters), constant wind speed assumed (no wind in the weather file),
     `pvsystem.pvwatts_dc` (gamma -0.4 %/K), `pvsystem.pvwatts_losses` with the PVWatts default loss items (14.08 %), and
     `inverter.pvwatts` (nominal efficiency 0.96, DC/AC ratio 1.2 so peaks above 1/1.2 of kWp are clipped).
Not modelled: shading from the actual surroundings, horizon, snow beyond the loss item, module degradation, real wind. Results are
modeled (D-021) and depend on assumed parameters; the annual specific yield is a plausibility check, not a validation against
measured PV output.

Input timestamps are the START of the hour (UTC), as in weather_klo_2023_hourly.csv (D-009); irradiance is the hourly mean,
so the sun position is taken at start + 30 min.

Task B3: assumed-PV scenario inputs (M-003). Writes, under data/canonical/pv/:
  pv_ac_w_per_kwp_2023_hourly.csv   inverter AC output per kWp in W/kW (CityLearn solar_generation convention), 8,760 hours
  pv_capacity_2023.json             per building and yield-to-demand ratio (0.5, 1.0, 1.5): kWp, cap, binding flag, annual yield
Classification: modeled (irradiance measured, conversion modeled) + assumed-parameter badge (D-021). No building has known PV
except by survey (SFH-low: no); SFH-mid and SFH-high are unknown (ISS-021), so every building gets the SCENARIO PV and the scenario
is "with assumed PV". Annual demand = non-shiftable load + heat-pump electricity under no control (ALG-001), from DER-009.
Run: cl/bin/python -I swiss/pipeline/build_pv.py

code.source:
M-005 single-node (1R1C) building thermal model, equation (1) of Melillo et al. 2021 (J. Phys.: Conf. Ser. 2042 012009), per floor area:
    C dT/dt = -H (T - T_amb) + g I + L_emitter + L_internal
Pooled per-m2 priors (owner decision 2026-11-18): the same H, g, C and internal gain per m2 for every building; only the EFFECTIVE AREA of a
building is calibrated, so that the model with ideal control at the setpoint reproduces the building's annual derived heat demand (energy
closure; the derived heat is itself SPF-anchored, M-001, ISS-028). All priors are assumptions or unverified; the model is labelled synthetic.
The step is the exact solution for piecewise-constant inputs over one step (no integration error):
    T_{k+1} = T_inf + (T_k - T_inf) exp(-dt / tau),   tau = C / H,   T_inf = T_amb + (g I + L_internal + L_emitter) / H
Units here: power in kW, areas in m2, H in W/(K m2), C in J/(K m2), I in W/m2, time step in seconds.

B7: pooled per-m2 RC parameters (M-005) and per-building effective area (energy closure with the derived heat, D-038).
Output: data/canonical/rc/rc_params_2023.json   Run: cl/bin/python -I swiss/pipeline/build_rc_params.py

M-005 in CityLearn 3.3.0: a DynamicsBuilding whose indoor temperature follows the single-node RC model (swiss/models/rc_building.py).

Extension by subclassing (CityLearn itself is not edited). Mapping of CityLearn semantics:
  heating_demand[t]            = heat delivered to the room in step t (kWh_th per step = kW at 3600 s); set by the `heating_device` action as
                                 action x nominal electric power x COP(T_out), exactly as CityLearn's LSTM building does for its own demand.
  tank discharge                serves part of that demand (stock logic); the device supplies the rest plus tank charging.
  indoor_dry_bulb_temperature[t] = temperature at the END of step t after the heat of step t (RC exact step).
Solar input of the RC equation is global horizontal irradiance = direct (beam horizontal) + diffuse of the weather file.

M-007.summary: A building with a cooled fraction f cooled by room units, the rest floating. Exact perfect-foresight optimum of the BILL for a Phase C cell (climate scenario x cooling adoption), S3 district with cooling (WP2).

Extends swiss/experiments/oracle_rc.py (not changed): the same per-building linear program over the year (tanks, battery, single-node RC room, export 8 Rp/kWh), plus
  Qc >= 0   heat removed from the room (kWh thermal per step) in COOLED buildings only; electricity Qc / COPc, COPc = CityLearn Carnot-fraction cooling COP at the outdoor
            temperature; capacity = nominal electric power x step x COPc, zero when the outdoor temperature is below 15 C (rc_building.COOLING_MIN_OUTDOOR_C, A-040)
  T_t = e T_{t-1} + (1 - e) [T_amb + (g A I + L A + 1000 (Q - Qc)) / H]                      (the RC step with net heat Q - Qc)
Comfort (hard constraints, as oracle_rc; the MPC uses soft ones):
  cooled buildings   lower 21 C; upper 24 C in the heating season and 26 C in the cooling season (June to September, local months), never below the thermostat path T_th
  uncooled buildings  unchanged from oracle_rc: lower 21 C, upper 24 C (never below T_th); they have no cooling variable and float in summer
  T_th = thermostat baseline (rc_building.simulate_thermostat): heat to 21 C, cool to 26 C if a cooling device exists; the baseline bill uses it, tanks and battery idle
Flexibility settings: 'band' (flexible, above), 'no thermal flexibility' (oracle_rc definition: lower 21 C, upper = max(21 C, T_th)) and 'pinned' (T equal to the thermostat path:
no building mass flexibility at all; the difference to 'band' is what thermal mass adds).
Inputs come from the cell's CityLearn dataset (swiss/datasets/climate/<scenario>_<adoption>/, swiss/pipeline/build_climate_datasets.py): weather, COP, tanks, PV, tariff and
carbon from the dataset; building areas from the dataset's RC parameters (the 2023-calibrated areas stay fixed in every scenario: the building does not change with the climate).
Household base load = non-shiftable load + DHW demand / DHW COP (the zero-action electricity of everything except space heat and PV; equal to oracle_rc's `net_s0 - derived heat / cop`).
Replay: the optimum is played in CityLearn through the combined `cooling_or_heating_device` action (negative = cooling); stop condition as Phase B: more than 0.5 % of the saving apart.

Run: PYTHONPATH=. cl/bin/python swiss/experiments/oracle_climate.py --cell hist_high [--band band] [--replay 5100]
Output: swiss/experiments/oracle_results/climate/<cell>__<band>.json (and .npz with the schedules if --save-schedules)

Controllers for the Phase C cells (WP3): thermostat with cooling, PV rule with cooling, receding-horizon MPC with a cooling variable.

Cells are S3 districts (PV, battery, RC building) with cooling in the cooled buildings (swiss/pipeline/build_climate_datasets.py); cooled buildings have the combined action
`cooling_or_heating_device` (positive = heating share of the heating capacity, negative = cooling share of the cooling capacity), the others `heating_device`.
  ThermostatAgentCool  heat to 21 C, cool to 26 C (the reference of every cell; identical to the thermostat baseline of oracle_climate)
  PVRuleCool           PVRule of rl.py (tanks charge 10-16 h, discharge 17-22 h, battery follows the PV surplus) on top of the cooling thermostat
  MPCClimate           receding-horizon MPC (mpc.MPCAgent machinery: horizon LP per building, optional district peak term, comfort margin, online model correction) with the
                       cooling variable Qc (heat removed, electricity Qc / COPc, capacity cooling_capacity_kwh), comfort lower 21 C (+ margin), upper 24 C in the heating season and
                       26 C in the cooling season (soft, high penalty), uncooled buildings float.
Forecasts (ClimateForecaster): 'perfect', or 'weather' = gradient boosting on calendar and weather features trained on the cell's own scenario (or another scenario for the
robustness test) outside the test weeks +- 1 week; the weather itself is taken as KNOWN over the horizon (A-028) unless a forecast-weather override is given (synthetic error,
labelled). Assumptions: docs/phases/phase_c_drafts/wp3_registry_draft.md.

D-009.summary: MeteoSwiss hourly `reference_timestamp` is treated as the END of the interval;

fields.Decision: MeteoSwiss hourly `reference_timestamp` is treated as the END of the interval; value for hour starting at UTC t = row labelled t+1h.
fields.Rationale: Mean July global radiation peaks at label 12:00 UTC; solar noon at Kloten ~11:26 UTC (equation of time ~-6 min) so peak hour interval is [11,12]. Not stated in the docs pages I could read. HEAPO's weather file uses the raw end labels as its Timestamp (its 8jB series equals KLO exactly with no relabel).
fields.Alternatives: Treat label as interval start
fields.Consequences: If wrong, weather is 1 h late relative to demand. Confirm against MeteoSwiss ODD documentation.

fields.Decision: PROPOSED carbon input (replaces Electricity Maps, D-005 fallback): MODELED hourly consumption-based lifecycle carbon intensity for CH 2023, reconstructed as I_t = [sum_tech gen_CH,tech,t * EF_tech + sum_n max(flow_n,t,0) * I_n,t] / [sum gen_CH + sum max(flow,0)], where I_n,t = generation-weighted lifecycle intensity of neighbour n (FR, DE, AT, IT) from its own public_power by technology (first-order tracing: ignores neighbours' own imports). Pumped-storage generation/consumption excluded from supply and load. Emission factors: IPCC AR5 WG3 Annex III lifecycle medians (nuclear 12, hydro 24, wind 11-12, solar PV 41-48, biomass 230, gas CC 490, coal 820 gCO2eq/kWh) or KBOB if obtainable - VALUES TO BE VERIFIED FROM THE SOURCE BEFORE USE. Also keep a domestic-generation-only intensity series as diagnostic. Method check: run the same reconstruction for 2016-2017 and compare with the EPFL hourly dataset (SRC-009): shape, seasonal and diurnal pattern, bias. Registered as modeled; average (not marginal) intensity.
fields.Rationale: Electricity Maps paid (user); HoroCarbon only a multi-year average; Energy-Charts is open (CC BY 4.0), keyless, has 2016 and 2023 hourly Swiss generation by technology, 15-min cross-border flows, and neighbours' generation
fields.Alternatives: Fixed annual factor; EPFL 2016-17 profile repeated for 2023 (not allowed by D-005); HoroCarbon average profile
fields.Consequences: Not full flow-tracing; Swiss data may omit small generation; emission factors are generic not Swiss-specific; result is a reconstruction not a measurement
fields.Status: accepted 2026-11-16 (user), together with the bulk download; emission-factor values must still be verified from the source before use

D-017.summary: PROPOSED storage assumption for Phase A (ISS-029).

fields.Decision: PROPOSED storage assumption for Phase A (ISS-029). Options: (1) synthetic thermal tanks (heating buffer for all six; DHW tank only where the HP serves the baseline load), capacities from stated volume x 1.163 Wh/(L K) x delta-T, labelled synthetic, with x0.5/x2 sensitivity [recommended]; (2) CityLearn-style 'hours of demand' sizing (simple, physically oversized: 2 h of p99 heat demand is 26-34 kWh_th for houses vs about 3-14 kWh_th for real 300-500 L tanks); (3) no storage in Phase A - run uncontrolled/BAU baselines only, move controllable assets to Phase B with PV and battery; (4) add battery now (Phase B scope, not recommended).
fields.Rationale: Controllers act only through storage devices
fields.Consequences: Option 1 adds ~assumed devices not in the data; option 3 is cleanest scientifically but gives no controller comparison

D-030.title: RL protocol on the Swiss environment (swiss/experiments/rl.py).
D-030.summary: RL protocol on the Swiss environment (swiss/experiments/rl.py).

fields.Decision: RL protocol on the Swiss environment (swiss/experiments/rl.py). Held-out weeks first (8 test weeks spread over the year, 44 training weeks); quarter cross-validation is implemented as a setting (protocol quarter, folds 1 to 4) for later. Training episodes are random 4-week windows that never touch a test step. Evaluation starts each window from a 96-step warm-up, scores only the window, and reports the cost corrected for stored heat as a range next to the raw cost. SAC and MARLISA bootstrap at window ends instead of treating them as terminal. The exact perfect-foresight cost optimum (swiss/experiments/oracle.py, replay-validated in CityLearn) is the ceiling: 299 CHF a year (0.84 % of the bill) at the assumed tank sizes, 0.57 % to 2.17 % for tanks 0.5 to 8 times the size.
fields.Rationale: User decisions in chat (held-out weeks now, quarter cross-validation later, do the episode-end fixes and the exact optimum); the first design (one-week episodes from empty tanks, window end terminal) made every rule look 1.5 % worse than over the year and taught SAC that stored heat is worthless (Pardo et al. 2017)
fields.Alternatives: One-week episodes from empty tanks (rejected: boundary artefacts); full-year episodes (memorisation, slow); valuing stored heat with a single number (rejected: the value is uncertain and as large as the whole saving)
fields.Consequences: The cost saving available to any controller is below 0.9 % of the bill, so RL results are read against that ceiling. The reward choice (R-001 or cost-dominant, D-023) is still open

Accounting is done outside CityLearn because CityLearn 3.3.0 prices imports only (cost = max(net, 0) x price): bill = import cost - export revenue (swiss/experiments/metrics.py, accounting.py); a replay test shows our import cost equals the environment's cost series (S0 35,750.32 CHF as in Phase A; S1 zero action 25,631.24 CHF). The reward cost term also ignores exports, so an export-aware reward preset is needed before RL on S1.

D-036.title: Ceiling gate result for the ladder (plan step 6, D-032 rule: RL only if the exact optimum saves at least 3 % of the bill).
D-036.summary: Ceiling gate result for the ladder (plan step 6, D-032 rule: RL only if the exact optimum saves at least 3 % of the bill).

fields.Decision: Ceiling gate result for the ladder (plan step 6, D-032 rule: RL only if the exact optimum saves at least 3 % of the bill). At the default assumed export price of 8 Rp/kWh: S1 (assumed PV) optimum saves 1,176 CHF = 6.03 % of its zero-action bill (19,510 CHF); S2 (assumed PV + battery 1 kWh/kWp) saves 3,043 CHF = 15.60 % (against the S1 zero-action bill the S2 optimum is 3,043 CHF lower, i.e. the same number because the zero-action bills coincide). Both PASS the gate; S1 also passes at 0, 4 and 12 Rp/kWh (7.98, 7.14, 4.51 %), S2 at all four (22.2, 19.4, 15.6, 10.4 %). Replay in CityLearn matches the programs to 0.00 CHF. RL on S1 and S2 is therefore authorised by the rule; scripts are written but not submitted (D-032 item 9).
fields.Rationale: rule D-032; evidence in docs/experiments/validation_reports/oracle_cost_bound_s1_s2.md and oracle_results/oracle_pvbat.json
fields.Alternatives: none
fields.Consequences: The ceilings depend on assumed PV, export price and battery (A-011 to A-017) and on synthetic tanks (ISS-032); shares are of a bill net of export revenue, so the same CHF looks larger as the export price rises. The exact optimum is a ceiling, not a forecast of what a learned controller reaches. Before RL on S1 or S2 the reward needs an export-aware preset (D-034)
fields.Status: accepted by rule (D-032), result stated in EL-0060

D-040.summary: B5 richer tariffs, scenario results (labelled what-ifs, S0 stays the realistic baseline).

fields.Decision: B2 15-minute pipeline and environment: data/canonical/q15 and CityLearn datasets at 900 s for S0 to S3 (DER-019, DER-020), every hourly series the exact aggregate of the 15-minute one, weather hourly information only (A-022, ISS-035), thermal split by proportional distribution (A-023), device sizes from 15-minute peaks (A-024). The stock zero-action run at 900 s gives 214,732.8 kWh and 35,752.99 CHF against 214,715.1 kWh and 35,750.32 CHF hourly (+0.008 %). Exact ceilings at 15 minutes: S0 0.87 %, S1 6.50 %, S2 16.16 %, S3 16.26 % (pure shifting) and 21.13 % (band 20-24), against 0.84, 6.03, 15.60, 15.96 and 20.85 % hourly. Replay of the first 4,000 steps matches the programs to 0.00 CHF for S1, S2 and S3 (both bands). Findings that needed code changes: a CityLearn tank action moves at most capacity x step length per step; CityLearn rescales loss_coefficient to the step length itself (schema value stays per hour); battery action is a fraction of nominal power x step length; devices must be sized on 15-minute peaks. 15-minute large files are regenerated by the pipeline, not tracked in git.
fields.Rationale: master plan B2, acceptance criteria 1 and 2
fields.Alternatives: tracked 15-minute data (about 160 MB, rejected)
fields.Consequences: A finer step adds little headroom with an hourly price and hourly weather; the contract bundle stays hourly (D-028 chunking not needed)

D-046.summary: Control-methods study and non-learning baseline (owner research request, protocol chosen by the agent): receding-horizon MPC that re-solves the exact-oracle LP (oracle_pvbat and oracle_rc programs) every hour from the CityLearn state, scored on the Phase B held-out weeks with the RL warm-up and scoring (rl.window_metrics), forecast ladder (perfect, same hour last week or day, weather-conditioned…

fields.Decision: Control-methods study and non-learning baseline (owner research request, protocol chosen by the agent): receding-horizon MPC that re-solves the exact-oracle LP (oracle_pvbat and oracle_rc programs) every hour from the CityLearn state, scored on the Phase B held-out weeks with the RL warm-up and scoring (rl.window_metrics), forecast ladder (perfect, same hour last week or day, weather-conditioned gradient boosting, synthetic noise), district peak term (joint LP), S3 comfort margin and online room-model correction, S1 to S3, run locally (3 to 15 min per configuration, no cluster). Results EXP-019, note docs/phases/control_methods_shortlist.md sections 6 to 9.
fields.Rationale: RL failed on the same weeks while the exact optimum passes the 3 % gate (D-044), so a method that shows how much of the headroom is reachable without perfect foresight was needed; MPC needs no training and uses the existing LP
fields.Alternatives: Imitation learning, residual RL, robust MPC, tuned rule only
fields.Consequences: Perfect-forecast MPC equals the exact ceiling (S2 14.60 % against 14.55 %); weather-conditioned forecasts reach 3.4 % (S1), 8.8 % (S2), 11.4 % (S3), the PV rule -0.2, 5.65, 6.05 %; history-only forecasts 3.7 % (S2); a district peak weight of 0.1 keeps the S2 saving and brings the highest hour from 117 kW to 63 kW (zero action 66 kW); S3 model error x0.8 gives 396 K h below 21 C, online correction plus a 0.2 C margin removes it for 0.8 point. Assumptions A-028 to A-031

fields.Consequences: Hourly scenario weather files DER-023 to DER-025 (tested, validated on 2023: reconstruction RMSE 1.40 K); assumptions A-032 to A-039; limitations in ISS-043 to ISS-045; the percentile rule needs the owner's confirmation

D-050.title: Cooling model and system archetypes.

fields.Decision: Cooling model and system archetypes. Cooling is a mode of the single-node RC model (M-006): a reversible heat pump with the rating, efficiency and 8 C supply temperature of the heating device, set point 26 C, off below 15 C outdoors (A-040 to A-043). Two archetypes: A central (whole building cooled; implemented and run) and B room units (cooled fraction f of the floor area, default f = 0.4 without a source, sensitivities 0.2 and 0.6; implemented in WP2b, results reported separately); reversible heat-pump supply-temperature variants (floor cooling at 16 to 18 C) and ground-source passive cooling are deferred by the owner's decision of 2026-11-19. Adoption by whole buildings from the shares of the 46 dwelling units: low = MFH-small (10.9 %), medium = MFH-medium (30.4 %), high = MFH-large (52.2 %), high_alt = MFH-medium + MFH-small + the three houses (47.8 %); these levels, the building assignment and the 26 C set point are labelled assumptions that the owner has not explicitly confirmed (A-042, A-044).
fields.Rationale: The proposal levels follow the sparse Swiss evidence (reported by search, not read: fewer than one in ten homes with fixed air conditioning, Empa projecting over 50 % of households with cooling later); no Swiss field data for set points or partial-room schedules was found
fields.Alternatives: Nested adoption levels; zone-split by area inside every building; a higher supply temperature
fields.Consequences: Cooling energy per cooled building differs between archetypes by construction and neither is validated (ISS-048); a level confounds adoption with building identity, so high_alt is run as a sensitivity
fields.Status: accepted (levels and set point pending owner confirmation)

Adoption by whole buildings from the shares of the 46 dwelling units: low = MFH-small (10.9 %), medium = MFH-medium (30.4 %), high = MFH-large (52.2 %), high_alt = MFH-medium + MFH-small + the three houses (47.8 %); these levels, the building assignment and the 26 C set point are labelled assumptions that the owner has not explicitly confirmed (A-042, A-044). | The proposal levels follow the sparse Swiss evidence (reported by search, not read: fewer than one in ten homes with fixed air conditioning, Empa projecting over 50 % of households with cooling later); no Swiss field data for set points or partial-room schedules was found | Nested adoption levels; zone-split by area inside every building; a higher supply temperature | Cooling energy per cooled building differs between archetypes by construction and neither is validated (ISS-048); a level confounds adoption with building identity, so high_alt is run as a sensitivity | accepted (levels and set point pending owner confirmation) |

D-051.summary: Evaluation design for Phase C: 26 cells (6 weather scenarios x adoption none, low, medium, high, plus high_alt for the two 3.0 C scenarios) plus archetype B (WP2b);

fields.Decision: Evaluation design for Phase C: 26 cells (6 weather scenarios x adoption none, low, medium, high, plus high_alt for the two 3.0 C scenarios) plus archetype B (WP2b); per cell the exact optimum of the S3 district with cooling with the band and pinned settings (mass value = pinned minus band), full-year rollouts of the thermostat and the replayed optimum with climate impact metrics, and on the eight held-out weeks (week 29 holds the heat wave) the thermostat, the PV rule, the MPC and the MPC with peak weight 0.1. No RL: no learner beat its reference in Phase B (D-044) and the gate of D-032 is met by the exact optimum, but classical control already reaches 75 to 77 % of it on the test weeks (EXP-023). The first MPC run let uncooled buildings overheat at no cost (free slack), which inflated its share of the ceiling; it was found before commit, replaced by the Phase B penalty of 0.05 CHF per K h and all MPC tasks were rerun (A-052).
fields.Rationale: Continuity with Phase B (ceiling-first, held-out weeks, bill scoring, thermostat reference); owner confirmed MPC as the controller family and dropped the residual RL test
fields.Alternatives: RL on the cooling cells; stochastic MPC (dropped in D-047)
fields.Consequences: Results EXP-021 to EXP-024 and docs/experiments/validation_reports/climate_matrix.md; headline: heating electricity falls 26 % from 2023 weather to 3.0 C, added cooling is small, mass value rises only slightly with cooling, PV covers most of the cooling electricity, uncooled-building overheating is a model artefact (ISS-046)

Sources searched 2026-11-19 (reported by search, not read in full): there is no official Swiss statistic of residential air-conditioning; estimates for today are about 5 % (Tages-Anzeiger / Der Bund, 2025), 10 % (a refrigeration-industry association, excluding homes with reversible heat pumps) and 4 to 10 % (Galaxus/YouGov survey, 533 Swiss respondents); about 20,000 split units are installed per year (Swissinfo). Future: Empa states that the share of households with cooling systems could rise above 50 % (scenario behind the figure not confirmed); the peer-reviewed benchmarking paper (Applied Energy, ScienceDirect article S0306261921001719) runs uptake from low to full with about 5 TWh in a moderate case and up to 17.5 TWh in 2050. No source found for a split by building type; regulation (neighbour consent, facade rules) is reported to make fixed units harder in apartments than in houses. So 10 % and 50 % are supported as endpoints (today's upper estimate; Empa's order of magnitude), 30 % is an interpolation, and the assignment of the cooled buildings (apartment blocks in the main cells, houses in high_alt) is not supported by a source.

The tank sizes themselves have no source: 300 L per house and 50 L per apartment unit are assumptions (D-017a) and the HEAPO survey records no tank data. Literature guidelines from other climates (about 70 L per kW of heat-pump capacity, Franco et al. 2021; 30 to 40 L per kW of total system water, Li et al. 2021) put 300 L at the low end for a 5 to 15 kW heat pump (that range is itself unsourced, ISS-030). The exact cost optimum (oracle_cost_bound.md) bounds the saving at 0.84 % of the bill at the assumed sizes and 2.17 % at eight times the size. Open until sizes are validated or varied.

CityLearn caps the cooling COP at 20 below the supply temperature, so cooling is disabled below 15 C outdoors (A-041). The replay equality of the exact optimum (0.000 % of the saving, cooled cells up to step 5,100 and the full year) checks the action mapping, not the physics, because the program and CityLearn share the RC step. The climate programs use the rounded dataset areas, which differ from oracle_rc by under 0.01 % of the bill for the heating-only cell (closed, documented).

R-001.title: `swiss.experiments.rewards.SwissDistrictReward` (D-019, accepted)
R-001.summary: reward_t = − Σ_k w_k · term_k(t) / scale_k, central agent, penalty-only.

fields.formula: reward_t = − Σ_k w_k · term_k(t) / scale_k, central agent, penalty-only.

terms.Unit: CHF per step (EKZ standard 2023, excl. VAT)
terms.Scale: mean per-step value under zero-action rollout

code.source:
Reward function R-001 for the Swiss heating district (Task A8, decision D-019).

Penalty-only, district level (central agent). Terms (each >= 0), each divided by a reference scale:
  cost   : sum_b max(net_b, 0) * electricity_pricing          [CHF per step]
  peak   : (max(sum_b net_b, 0))**2                           [kW^2, smooth surrogate of peak demand]
  ramp   : |sum_b net_b(t) - sum_b net_b(t-1)|                [kW]
  carbon : sum_b max(net_b, 0) * carbon_intensity             [only if the observation exists; weight 0 otherwise]
reward = - sum_k w_k * term_k / scale_k.   Scales = mean of each term under the uncontrolled (zero-action) rollout
(computed by run_baselines.py, stored in results/reward_scales.json).
A comfort term is deliberately ABSENT: the Phase A dataset has no thermal dynamics or measured indoor temperature, and
heating/DHW demand is always met, so a comfort penalty would be meaningless (D-018/D-019).

def terms(self, observations):
        net = np.array([o['net_electricity_consumption'] for o in observations], dtype=float)
        imp = np.maximum(net, 0.0)
        price = np.array([o['electricity_pricing'] for o in observations], dtype=float)
        district = float(net.sum())
        ramp = 0.0 if self._prev is None else abs(district - self._prev)
        self._prev = district
        carbon = 0.0
        if all('carbon_intensity' in o for o in observations):
            carbon = float((imp * np.array([o['carbon_intensity'] for o in observations], dtype=float)).sum())
        return {'cost': float((imp * price).sum()), 'peak': max(district, 0.0) ** 2, 'ramp': ramp, 'carbon': carbon}

  peak   : (max(sum_b net_b, 0))**2                           [kW^2, smooth surrogate of peak demand]
  ramp   : |sum_b net_b(t) - sum_b net_b(t-1)|                [kW]
  carbon : sum_b max(net_b, 0) * carbon_intensity             [only if the observation exists; weight 0 otherwise]
reward = - sum_k w_k * term_k / scale_k.   Scales = mean of each term under the uncontrolled (zero-action) rollout
(computed by run_baselines.py, stored in results/reward_scales.json).
A comfort term is deliberately ABSENT: the Phase A dataset has no thermal dynamics or measured indoor temperature, and
heating/DHW demand is always met, so a comfort penalty would be meaningless (D-018/D-019).

def terms(self, observations):
        net = np.array([o['net_electricity_consumption'] for o in observations], dtype=float)
        imp, exp = np.maximum(net, 0.0), np.maximum(-net, 0.0)
        price = np.array([o['electricity_pricing'] for o in observations], dtype=float)
        district = float(net.sum())
        ramp = 0.0 if self._prev is None else abs(district - self._prev)
        self._prev = district
        carbon = 0.0
        if all('carbon_intensity' in o for o in observations):
            carbon = float((imp * np.array([o['carbon_intensity'] for o in observations], dtype=float)).sum())
        comfort = 0.0
        if all('indoor_dry_bulb_temperature' in o for o in observations):
            comfort = float(np.maximum(self.setpoint - np.array([o['indoor_dry_bulb_temperature'] for o in observations], dtype=float), 0.0).sum())
        return {'cost': float((imp * price).sum() - self.export_price * exp.sum()), 'peak': max(district, 0.0) ** 2, 'ramp': ramp, 'carbon': carbon, 'comfort': comfort}

series:outdoor_temperature.title: Outdoor temperature (Zurich/Kloten)
series:outdoor_temperature.summary: Hourly air temperature measured by MeteoSwiss at Zurich/Kloten, used for all six buildings (D-010). Annual mean 11.6 °C, range -12.9 to 36.0 °C, 0 missing hours. MeteoSwiss labels each hour by its END; the series is shifted so that each value belongs to the hour that STARTS at the timestamp (D-009).

code.source:
Task A4/A6: hourly 2023 weather for Zurich/Kloten (KLO) from MeteoSwiss OGD.

Input : data/raw/meteoswiss/ogd-smn_klo_h_historical_2020-2029.csv  (SRC-004)
Output: data/canonical/weather_klo_2023_hourly.csv                   (DER-007)
        docs/data/data_quality_reports/qc_weather_klo_2023.json

Timestamp convention (D-009, determined empirically, see EL-0018): MeteoSwiss hourly
`reference_timestamp` (UTC) labels the END of the averaging hour. The value for the
hour that STARTS at UTC t is therefore the row labelled t+1h. Evidence: July mean global
radiation peaks at label 12:00 UTC while local solar noon at Kloten is ~11:26 UTC
(interval [11,12] centred 11:30).

Variables (all measured except the one derived column):
  temp_c (tre200h0), rh_pct (ure200h0), ghi_wm2 (gre000h0), diffuse_wm2 (ods000h0),
  sunshine_min (sre000h0), beam_horizontal_wm2 = ghi - diffuse   [DERIVED, horizontal
  beam component, NOT direct-normal irradiance].
No cleaning: night-time radiation of ~1-2 W/m2 (sensor offset) is kept as measured.

Run: cl/bin/python -I swiss/pipeline/build_weather.py

series:carbon_intensity.title: Grid carbon intensity (modeled)
series:carbon_intensity.summary: MODELED, not measured. Hourly lifecycle CO2 intensity of the electricity used in Switzerland, rebuilt from Energy-Charts generation and cross-border flow data (M-002). The yearly mean is 58.1 g/kWh, but do not read the level: the proxy emission factors alone move that mean between 47 and 69 g/kWh, and the level is only about 61% to 62% of the EPFL reference. A method check against the EPFL 2016-17 series agrees in shape (hourly r 0.98) but not in level (ratio of means 0.61 in 2016, 0.62 in 2017). Use it for relative signals only (D-013b).

code.source:
def intensity(df, solar_ef, proxy_scale=1.0):
    ef = dict(EF_IPCC); ef.update({k: v * proxy_scale for k, v in EF_PROXY.items()}); ef['Solar'] = solar_ef
    # technologies that are entirely absent (all NaN for the whole window) are not part of that system's mix
    df = df.dropna(axis=1, how='all')
    df = df.apply(structural_zero)
    cols = [c for c in df.columns if c not in EXCLUDE and c in ef]
    unknown = [c for c in df.columns if c not in EXCLUDE and c not in ef]
    assert not unknown, f'unmapped technologies: {unknown}'
    g = df[cols].clip(lower=0)
    # NaN in any generation column makes the hour NaN (no interpolation)
    tot = g.sum(axis=1, min_count=len(cols))
    emis = (g * pd.Series(ef)[cols]).sum(axis=1, min_count=len(cols))
    return emis / tot, tot, emis

Task A6 / D-013: modeled hourly consumption-based LIFECYCLE carbon intensity of the Swiss electricity supply.

Inputs : data/raw/energy_charts/*.json (SRC-011, CC BY 4.0, attribution energy-charts.info):
         public_power for ch/de/fr/at/it (MW) and cbpf (cross-border physical flows into CH, GW; positive = import into CH,
         sign convention verified: July 2023 net export of 56 GWh/day equals ch 'Cross border electricity trading').
Method (first-order tracing, average not marginal intensity):
  I_dom,t = sum_k G_k,t EF_k / sum_k G_k,t                       (Swiss domestic generation only; diagnostic series)
  I_n,t   = same formula for neighbour n (FR, DE, AT, IT) from its own generation (its own imports ignored)
  I_cons,t = [sum_k G_k,t EF_k + sum_n max(F_n,t,0) * I_n,t] / [sum_k G_k,t + sum_n max(F_n,t,0)]
  Exports leave at the average mix (do not change the intensity). Pumped-storage generation and consumption are excluded.
Emission factors: IPCC AR5 WG3 Annex III Table A.III.2 lifecycle medians (verified from the PDF) with documented PROXIES
for technologies absent from that table (see EF_PROXY). Output unit gCO2eq/kWh (and kg/kWh for CityLearn).
No interpolation: hours with missing inputs stay NaN and are counted.
Run: cl/bin/python -I swiss/pipeline/build_carbon.py [2023|2016|2017]

numbers.label: Mean with proxy factors halved / raised by half

caveats: Level is about 61%-62% of the EPFL reference: do not quote it as a Swiss grid intensity.
The yearly mean swings between 47 and 69 g/kWh depending on the proxy emission factors (halved or raised by half). The shape is reliable, the level is not.

For the apartment buildings, the non-heat-pump load is SYNTHETIC: apartment meters drawn at random from other EKZ buildings (D-006, D-015). card:building_selection.title: Building selection
card:building_selection.summary: How the six buildings were chosen from the HEAPO and EKZ candidate pools (D-006): rules fixed before looking at IDs, pools split into strata, and the building nearest each stratum median taken.

code.source:
def single_family():
    h = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(INT, 'heapo_candidates.csv'))
    pool = h[h.has_hp_submeter & (h.cov_2023 >= MIN_COV) & (h.cov_hp_2023 >= MIN_COV)
             & (h.Survey_HeatPump_Installation_Type == 'air-source')
             & (h.Survey_Building_Type == 'house') & h.Survey_Building_LivingArea.notna()
             & (h.n_dup_ts == 0)].copy()
    # three strata by terciles of 2023 heat-pump electricity
    q = pool.kwh_hp_2023.quantile([1 / 3, 2 / 3]).values
    pool['stratum'] = np.where(pool.kwh_hp_2023 <= q[0], 'low', np.where(pool.kwh_hp_2023 <= q[1], 'mid', 'high'))
    rows = []
    for s in ['low', 'mid', 'high']:
        r = nearest_to_median(pool[pool.stratum == s], 'kwh_hp_2023')
        rows.append({'role': f'SFH-{s}', 'source': 'HEAPO', 'id': int(r.Household_ID), 'stratum': s,
                     'n_pool': int((pool.stratum == s).sum()), 'kwh_total_2023': r.kwh_total_2023,
                     'kwh_hp_2023': r.kwh_hp_2023, 'area_m2': r.Survey_Building_LivingArea,
                     'residents': r.Survey_Building_Residents, 'pv_flag': r.Installation_HasPVSystem,
                     'units': 1})
    return rows, len(pool)

def multi_family():
    m = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(INT, 'ekz_meters.csv'))
    pool = m[(m['0_installation_type'] == 'Heat pump') & (m['0_object_type'] == 'Apartment building')
             & (m.cov_2023 >= MIN_COV) & (m.cov_2024 >= MIN_COV) & (m.n_dup_ts == 0)
             & (m['0_num_housing_units'] >= 4)].copy()
    bins = {'small': (4, 6), 'medium': (7, 14), 'large': (24, 10 ** 6)}
    rows = []
    for s, (lo, hi) in bins.items():
        sub = pool[(pool['0_num_housing_units'] >= lo) & (pool['0_num_housing_units'] <= hi)].copy()
        sub['kwh_per_unit'] = sub.kwh_import_2023 / sub['0_num_housing_units']
        r = nearest_to_median(sub, 'kwh_per_unit')
        rows.append({'role': f'MFH-{s}', 'source': 'EKZ', 'id': int(r['0_meter_id']), 'stratum': s,
                     'n_pool': len(sub), 'kwh_total_2023': np.nan, 'kwh_hp_2023': r.kwh_import_2023,
                     'area_m2': np.nan, 'residents': np.nan, 'pv_flag': np.nan,
                     'units': int(r['0_num_housing_units']), 'object_id': int(r['0_object_id'])})
    return rows, len(pool)

card:cop_model.title: Heat-pump COP and thermal demand
card:cop_model.summary: Heat delivered is not measured. It is derived from measured heat-pump electricity times a modeled COP whose Carnot fraction η is calibrated per building so the annual SPF matches Swiss field data (Arpagaus et al. 2023). The non-space-heating baseline of heat-pump electricity (warm-day mean, A-005) becomes the hot-water demand.

code.source:
def cop(t_out, eta, t_sup):
    t_out = np.asarray(t_out, dtype=float)
    with np.errstate(divide='ignore', invalid='ignore'):
        c = eta * (t_sup + 273.15) / (t_sup - t_out)
    c = np.where(c < 0, 20.0, c)
    c = np.where(c > 20, 20.0, c)
    return c

def calibrate_eta(elec, t_out, t_sup, spf_target, lo=0.05, hi=1.0):
    """eta such that sum(elec*cop)/sum(elec) = spf_target (bisection; monotone in eta)."""
    elec = np.asarray(elec, dtype=float)
    m = ~(np.isnan(elec) | np.isnan(t_out))
    e, t = elec[m], np.asarray(t_out)[m]
    f = lambda eta: (e * cop(t, eta, t_sup)).sum() / e.sum() - spf_target
    if f(lo) > 0 or f(hi) < 0:
        raise ValueError('spf_target not reachable within eta bounds')
    for _ in range(80):
        mid = (lo + hi) / 2
        lo, hi = (mid, hi) if f(mid) < 0 else (lo, mid)
    return (lo + hi) / 2

def split_baseline(e_hp, local_hour, temp_c, warm_threshold_c=16.0):
    """Split hourly HP electricity into a non-space-heating baseline and space heating.

    Baseline per day B = mean daily electricity on days with mean T >= warm_threshold_c.
    Hourly shape p(h) = mean warm-day profile by local hour (normalised to sum 1).
    E_base(t) = min(E(t), B * p(hour(t))) ; E_sh = E - E_base.  Returns (e_base, e_sh, B_kwh_day).
    """
    import pandas as pd
    s = pd.Series(np.asarray(e_hp, dtype=float), index=e_hp.index)
    days = s.index.tz_convert('Europe/Zurich').floor('1D')
    tmean = pd.Series(np.asarray(temp_c, dtype=float), index=s.index).groupby(days).transform('mean')
    warm = (tmean >= warm_threshold_c).to_numpy()
    full = s.groupby(days).transform(lambda x: x.notna().all()).to_numpy().astype(bool)
    ok = warm & full
    B = float(s[ok].groupby(days[ok]).sum().mean())
    prof = s[ok].groupby(s.index.tz_convert('Europe/Zurich').hour[ok]).mean()
    prof = prof / prof.sum()
    hours = s.index.tz_convert('Europe/Zurich').hour
    base = np.minimum(s.to_numpy(), B * prof.reindex(hours).to_numpy())
    base = pd.Series(base, index=s.index)
    return base, s - base, B

Task A5: derive heating and DHW thermal demand (model M-001, D-014) for the six buildings.

Inputs : data/canonical/hourly/<role>_2023_hourly.csv (DER-005), weather_klo_2023_hourly.csv (DER-007)
Outputs: data/canonical/thermal/<role>_2023_thermal_hourly.csv (DER-009), thermal_params.json,
         docs/data/data_quality_reports/qc_thermal_2023.json

All thermal quantities are DERIVED (electricity x modeled COP), not measured.
Parameters (D-014d): supply T: SH 35 C (SFH floor heating) / 45 C (MFH assumption), DHW 55 C;
SPF targets (Arpagaus et al. 2023, IEA HPC paper 478, Table 1): SFH SH-only 3.7; MFH combined 3.1 (renovation
class); DHW-mode SPF 2.8 for all.  eta calibrated per building (annual).

Run: cl/bin/python -I swiss/pipeline/build_thermal_demand.py

card:cop_model.formula: COP = η · (T_sup + 273.15) / (T_sup − T_out);  Q_thermal = E_HP · COP
caveats: The planned linearity diagnostic (derived heat vs heating degree-days) was found NOT to be a valid test of the COP model; see the addendum in qc_thermal_2023.md.
The COP curve is capped at twenty when the outdoor temperature approaches the supply temperature: 120 h (SFH-low), 124 h (SFH-mid), 104 h (SFH-high) in 2023.
Single supply temperature per mode, no defrost and no part-load behaviour (model registry limitations).

card:tanks.title: Thermal storage tanks (synthetic)
card:tanks.summary: SYNTHETIC. No building has documented storage; tank sizes come from the sizing rule in D-017a (heating buffer for all six; hot-water tank only where the heat pump serves a hot-water load). Sensitivity runs halve and double the sizes.

code.source:
def main(tank_scale=1.0, out_name='swiss_district_2023', carbon_file=None, tank_eff=TANK_EFF, thermal_subdir='thermal', pv_ratio=None, battery_kwh_per_kwp=None, rc=False, q15=False,
         weather_file=None, pv_file=None, cooled_buildings=(), climate_scenario=None, cooled_fraction=1.0):
    out_dir = os.path.join(ROOT, 'swiss', 'datasets', out_name)
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    params = json.load(open(os.path.join(CAN, thermal_subdir, 'thermal_params.json')))
    # B2: q15 = 900 s steps from the 15-minute pipeline (data/canonical/q15, swiss/pipeline/build_15min.py); the default stays the hourly dataset
    dt_h = 0.25 if q15 else 1.0
    qd = os.path.join(CAN, 'q15')
    # Phase C (WP2): scenario weather / PV files (hourly, same columns and 2023 time stamps as the canonical ones) and cooled buildings; defaults leave every Phase A and B build unchanged
    assert weather_file is None or not q15, 'scenario weather files are hourly (Phase C)'
    cooled_buildings = tuple(cooled_buildings)
    assert all(r in ROLES for r in cooled_buildings), f'unknown role in {cooled_buildings}'
    assert not cooled_buildings or rc, 'cooling needs the RC thermal model (--rc)'
    w = pd.read_csv(weather_file if weather_file else (os.path.join(qd, 'weather_klo_2023_15min.csv') if q15 else os.path.join(CAN, 'weather_klo_2023_hourly.csv')), index_col='timestamp_utc', parse_dates=True)
    tar = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(qd, 'tariff_ekz_standard_2023_15min.csv') if q15 else os.path.join(CAN, 'tariff_ekz_standard_2023_hourly.csv'), index_col='timestamp_utc', parse_dates=True)
    idx = w.index
    loc = idx.tz_convert('Europe/Zurich')
    cal = pd.DataFrame({'month': loc.month, 'hour': loc.hour + 1, 'day_type': loc.dayofweek + 1,
                        'daylight_savings_status': np.array([int(t.dst().total_seconds() > 0) for t in loc])}, index=idx)
    if q15:
        cal['minutes'] = loc.minute
    loss_coeff = LOSS_COEFF      # per HOUR: CityLearn's StorageDevice.loss_coefficient property rescales it to the step length itself (1 - (1 - c) ** step_hours)

    def ahead(s, k):  # exact future value (perfect foresight); last k hours repeat the final value
        return s.shift(-k).ffill()

    weather = pd.DataFrame({
        'outdoor_dry_bulb_temperature': w.temp_c, 'outdoor_relative_humidity': w.rh_pct,
        'diffuse_solar_irradiance': w.diffuse_wm2.fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0),
        'direct_solar_irradiance': w.beam_horizontal_wm2.fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0)})
    for c in list(weather.columns):
        for k in (1, 2, 3):
            weather[f'{c}_predicted_{k}'] = ahead(weather[c], k)
    weather.to_csv(os.path.join(out_dir, 'weather.csv'), index=False)

    price = pd.DataFrame({'electricity_pricing': tar.total_chf_kwh})
    for k in (1, 2, 3):
        price[f'electricity_pricing_predicted_{k}'] = ahead(price['electricity_pricing'], k)
    price.to_csv(os.path.join(out_dir, 'pricing.csv'), index=False)

    carbon_ref = None
    if carbon_file:
        pd.read_csv(carbon_file).to_csv(os.path.join(out_dir, 'carbon_intensity.csv'), index=False)
        carbon_ref = 'carbon_intensity.csv'

    pv_w = pv_caps = None
    if pv_ratio is not None:   # B3: assumed-PV scenario (M-003); default build is unchanged
        pv_w = pd.read_csv(pv_file if pv_file else (os.path.join(qd, 'pv_ac_w_per_kwp_2023_15min.csv') if q15 else os.path.join(CAN, 'pv', 'pv_ac_w_per_kwp_2023_hourly.csv')), index_col='timestamp_utc', parse_dates=True).pv_ac_w_per_kwp
        assert (pv_w.index == idx).all()
        pv_caps = json.load(open(os.path.join(CAN, 'pv', 'pv_capacity_2023.json')))['buildings']

    if battery_kwh_per_kwp is not None:
        assert pv_ratio is not None, 'the battery rule is defined per kWp of PV (B4): pass --pv-ratio too'
    rc_params = None
    if rc:   # B7: single-node RC thermal model (M-005, D-038); per-building effective area from the energy closure
        from swiss.models.rc_building import simulate_ideal
        rc_params = json.load(open(os.path.join(CAN, 'rc', 'rc_params_2023.json')))
        rc_ghi = (w.beam_horizontal_wm2.fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0) + w.diffuse_wm2.fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0)).to_numpy()
    buildings, manifest = {}, {}
    for i, role in enumerate(ROLES, 1):
        d = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(qd, 'thermal', f'{role}_2023_thermal_15min.csv') if q15 else os.path.join(CAN, thermal_subdir, f'{role}_2023_thermal_hourly.csv'), index_col='timestamp_utc', parse_dates=True)
        assert (d.index == idx).all()
        dh = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(CAN, thermal_subdir, f'{role}_2023_thermal_hourly.csv'), index_col='timestamp_utc', parse_dates=True)   # device sizes always from the hourly series
        name = f'Building_{i}'
        rc_q = rc_T = None
        if rc:
            rc_q, rc_T = simulate_ideal(rc_params['buildings'][role]['effective_area_m2'], w.temp_c.to_numpy(), rc_ghi, dt_s=3600.0 * dt_h)
            rc_q = rc_q * dt_h                      # kW -> kWh per step
        es = pd.DataFrame({
            'month': cal.month, 'hour': cal.hour, 'day_type': cal.day_type,
            'daylight_savings_status': cal.daylight_savings_status,
            'indoor_dry_bulb_temperature': SETPOINT_C if rc_T is None else rc_T,
            'non_shiftable_load': d.non_shiftable_load_kwh, 'dhw_demand': d.dhw_demand_kwh,
            'cooling_demand': 0.0, 'heating_demand': d.heating_demand_kwh if rc_q is None else rc_q, 'solar_generation': 0.0 if pv_w is None else pv_w.to_numpy(),
            'indoor_dry_bulb_temperature_cooling_set_point': 26.0,
            'indoor_dry_bulb_temperature_heating_set_point': SETPOINT_C, 'hvac_mode': 3 if role in cooled_buildings else 2})
        if q15:
            es['minutes'] = cal.minutes
        es.to_csv(os.path.join(out_dir, f'{name}.csv'), index=False)
        p = params[role]
        # device size = 1.1 x the highest power seen at the dataset's own resolution (kW): the 15-minute series has higher power peaks than the hourly one, and a device
        # sized on hourly peaks could not supply the derived 15-minute heat demand (the 15-minute exact optimum was infeasible in that case)
        src = d if q15 else dh
        peak_sh = float(src.e_hp_space_heating_kwh.max() / dt_h); peak_dhw = float(src.e_hp_baseline_kwh.max() / dt_h)
        sh_cap = buffer_kwh(role) * tank_scale
        mean_dhw_day = float(dh.dhw_demand_kwh.sum() / 365.0)
        b = {'type': 'citylearn.building.Building', 'include': True, 'energy_simulation': f'{name}.csv',
             'weather': 'weather.csv', 'carbon_intensity': carbon_ref, 'pricing': 'pricing.csv',
             'inactive_observations': [], 'inactive_actions': [],
             'heating_device': {'type': 'citylearn.energy_model.HeatPump', 'autosize': False,
                                'attributes': {'nominal_power': round(peak_sh * 1.1, 4), 'efficiency': round(p['eta_sh'], 6),
                                               'target_heating_temperature': p['T_sup_sh_c'], 'target_cooling_temperature': 8.0}},
             'dhw_device': {'type': 'citylearn.energy_model.HeatPump', 'autosize': False,
                            'attributes': {'nominal_power': round(max(peak_dhw * 1.1, 0.01), 4), 'efficiency': round(p['eta_dhw'], 6),
                                           'target_heating_temperature': p['T_sup_dhw_c'], 'target_cooling_temperature': 8.0}},
             'heating_storage': {'type': 'citylearn.energy_model.StorageTank', 'autosize': False,
                                 'attributes': {'capacity': round(sh_cap, 4), 'efficiency': tank_eff, 'loss_coefficient': loss_coeff}}}
        if pv_w is not None:
            kwp = pv_caps[role]['ratios'][str(float(pv_ratio))]['kwp']
            b['pv'] = {'type': 'citylearn.energy_model.PV', 'autosize': False, 'attributes': {'nominal_power': kwp}}
        bat_kwh = 0.0
        if battery_kwh_per_kwp is not None:   # B4: assumed battery per building (M-004), constant efficiency, no degradation
            bat_kwh = round(b['pv']['attributes']['nominal_power'] * battery_kwh_per_kwp, 4)
            eta = BATTERY['efficiency']
            b['electrical_storage'] = {'type': 'citylearn.energy_model.Battery', 'autosize': False,
                                       'attributes': {'capacity': bat_kwh, 'nominal_power': round(bat_kwh * BATTERY['c_rate'], 4),
                                                      'depth_of_discharge': BATTERY['depth_of_discharge'], 'efficiency': eta,
                                                      'loss_coefficient': 0.0, 'capacity_loss_coefficient': 0.0,
                                                      'power_efficiency_curve': [[0.0, eta], [1.0, eta]],
                                                      'capacity_power_curve': [[0.0, 1.0], [1.0, 1.0]]}}
        dhw_cap = 0.0
        if mean_dhw_day >= DHW_MIN_KWH_DAY:
            dhw_cap = mean_dhw_day * tank_scale
            b['dhw_storage'] = {'type': 'citylearn.energy_model.StorageTank', 'autosize': False,
                                'attributes': {'capacity': round(dhw_cap, 4), 'efficiency': tank_eff, 'loss_coefficient': loss_coeff}}
        if role in cooled_buildings:   # Phase C: reversible heat pump = a cooling device of the same rating, efficiency and supply temperature as the heating device (A-040)
            b['cooling_device'] = {'type': 'citylearn.energy_model.HeatPump', 'autosize': False, 'attributes': dict(b['heating_device']['attributes'])}
            if cooled_fraction < 1.0:   # archetype B (room units, WP2b, A-058): the units cover a fraction of the floor area, so their capacity is proportional to it
                b['cooling_device']['attributes']['nominal_power'] = round(b['heating_device']['attributes']['nominal_power'] * cooled_fraction, 6)
            b['inactive_actions'] = ['heating_device']          # cooled buildings use the combined action: negative = cooling, positive = heating (CityLearn forbids both)
        elif cooled_buildings:
            b['inactive_actions'] = ['cooling_or_heating_device']
        if rc:
            b['type'] = 'swiss.citylearn_build.rc_dynamics.RCDynamicsBuilding'
            b['dynamics'] = {'type': 'swiss.citylearn_build.rc_dynamics.RCDynamics',
                             'attributes': {'area_eff': rc_params['buildings'][role]['effective_area_m2'], 'filename': 'rc_params.json'}}
            if role in cooled_buildings and cooled_fraction < 1.0:   # archetype B: two independent zones (swiss/citylearn_build/rc_dynamics.py); omitted for archetype A so its datasets stay identical
                b['dynamics']['attributes']['cooled_fraction'] = cooled_fraction
        buildings[name] = b
        manifest[name] = {'role': role, 'heating_tank_kwh_th': round(sh_cap, 3), 'dhw_tank_kwh_th': round(dhw_cap, 3),
                          'hp_sh_nominal_kw': b['heating_device']['attributes']['nominal_power'],
                          'hp_dhw_nominal_kw': b['dhw_device']['attributes']['nominal_power']}
        if cooled_buildings:
            manifest[name]['cooled'] = role in cooled_buildings
            if role in cooled_buildings:
                manifest[name]['cooling_device_nominal_kw'] = b['cooling_device']['attributes']['nominal_power']
                if cooled_fraction < 1.0:
                    manifest[name]['cooled_fraction'] = cooled_fraction
        if pv_w is not None:
            manifest[name]['pv_kwp'] = b['pv']['attributes']['nominal_power']
        if battery_kwh_per_kwp is not None:
            manifest[name]['battery_kwh'] = bat_kwh
    observations = {k: {'active': k in ('day_type', 'hour', 'outdoor_dry_bulb_temperature', 'net_electricity_consumption',
                                         'electricity_pricing', 'electricity_pricing_predicted_1', 'electricity_pricing_predicted_2',
                                         'electricity_pricing_predicted_3', 'heating_storage_soc', 'dhw_storage_soc') or (k == 'electrical_storage_soc' and battery_kwh_per_kwp is not None) or (k == 'indoor_dry_bulb_temperature' and rc),
                    'shared_in_central_agent': k in ('day_type', 'hour', 'outdoor_dry_bulb_temperature', 'electricity_pricing',
                                                      'electricity_pricing_predicted_1', 'electricity_pricing_predicted_2',
                                                      'electricity_pricing_predicted_3')}
                    for k in ['day_type', 'hour', 'outdoor_dry_bulb_temperature'] + (['indoor_dry_bulb_temperature'] if rc else []) + ['net_electricity_consumption', 'electricity_pricing',
                              'electricity_pricing_predicted_1', 'electricity_pricing_predicted_2', 'electricity_pricing_predicted_3',
                              'heating_storage_soc', 'dhw_storage_soc', 'electrical_storage_soc']}
    actions = {'heating_storage': {'active': True}, 'dhw_storage': {'active': True}, 'electrical_storage': {'active': battery_kwh_per_kwp is not None},
               'cooling_storage': {'active': False}, 'cooling_device': {'active': False}, 'heating_device': {'active': rc},
               'cooling_or_heating_device': {'active': bool(cooled_buildings)}}
    schema = {'random_seed': 0, 'central_agent': True, 'simulation_start_time_step': 0, 'simulation_end_time_step': len(idx) - 1,
              'episode_time_steps': None, 'rolling_episode_split': False, 'random_episode_split': False,
              'seconds_per_time_step': 3600.0 * dt_h, 'observations': observations, 'actions': actions,
              'reward_function': {'type': 'citylearn.reward_function.RewardFunction', 'attributes': {}},
              'buildings': buildings, 'root_directory': '.'}   # '.' = the schema's own folder (CityLearn 3.3.0 resolves it relative to schema.json), so the dataset is portable
    json.dump(schema, open(os.path.join(out_dir, 'schema.json'), 'w'), indent=1)
    json.dump(manifest, open(os.path.join(out_dir, 'build_manifest.json'), 'w'), indent=1)
    if climate_scenario is not None or weather_file or pv_file or cooled_buildings:   # Phase C: what this dataset is made of (kept outside build_manifest.json, which lists buildings only)
        json.dump({'climate_scenario': climate_scenario, 'weather_file': os.path.relpath(weather_file, ROOT) if weather_file else None,
                   'pv_file': os.path.relpath(pv_file, ROOT) if pv_file else None, 'cooled_buildings': list(cooled_buildings), 'pv_ratio': pv_ratio,
                   'battery_kwh_per_kwp': battery_kwh_per_kwp, 'rc': rc, 'cooling_set_point_c': 26.0, 'cooling_device_supply_c': 8.0,
                   'archetype': 'room units' if cooled_fraction < 1.0 else 'central', 'cooled_fraction': cooled_fraction},
                  open(os.path.join(out_dir, 'build_meta.json'), 'w'), indent=1)
    if rc:
        json.dump(rc_params, open(os.path.join(out_dir, 'rc_params.json'), 'w'), indent=1)
    print(json.dumps(manifest, indent=1))
    return out_dir
